QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_38

question.text: Krishna Capital Cat II AIF realises INR 60 crore from the sale of a portfolio company in which it invested INR 25 crore. The fund's waterfall provides for 100% return of capital, 8% preferred return (cumulative INR 5 crore already hit via prior distributions), and 80/20 carry thereafter with a full GP catch-up. Focusing ONLY on THIS exit (assume capital fully returned via this exit and pref is met mid-way), what is the GP's INDICATIVE carry on this INR 60 crore if the incremental profit beyond capital + pref is INR 30 crore?

answer.text: INR 6 crore (20% of INR 30 crore incremental profit).

explanation.text: The Logic: With 100% catch-up and 80/20 carry, the GP ultimately takes 20% of CUMULATIVE profits above capital (net of hurdle mechanics). On incremental profit of INR 30 crore attributable to this exit (beyond capital and pref), GP carry = 20% x 30 = INR 6 crore. Catch-up simply accelerates GP's share during the pref zone; across the full profit, the ratio is 80/20. The Trap: 40% would be if the question implied a 60/40 split (not standard). 10% misses catch-up. 25% of gross proceeds (INR 60 cr) ignores return-of-capital and pref. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests identical math. XIX-A LP-side version tests 'carry as % of profit' in plain-English framing. Manager's Pro-Tip: Show LPs a sample waterfall on a hypothetical '2x exit' and '3x exit' in the PPM appendix. Transparency up-front means fewer audit-season disputes when real carry gets accrued on the GAAP books.
